title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper FaSTCC: Fast Sparse Tensor Contractions on CPUs
problem: Evaluation and validation of sparse tensor contraction implementations on CPUs
motivation: Reproducibility of artifacts is critical for scientific computing; formal evaluation of FaSTCC's claims and implementation details
method: This report evaluates whether the FaSTCC code—which performs sparse tensor contractions, a mathematical operation that efficiently combines multi-dimensional arrays when most values are zero—produces the same performance results as the original paper reported. The researchers ran the implementation on CPUs following the SC25 Reproducibility Initiative's systematic testing approach, checking performance across different systems and comparing actual speedups to those claimed in the original work. They verified whether the optimization approach actually works and whether the performance improvements hold up in practice.
key_novelty: This work independently tests whether FaSTCC's sparse tensor contraction implementation on CPUs actually achieves the performance improvements claimed in the original paper.
contributions: Systematic artifact evaluation for FaSTCC sparse tensor contractions
Reproducibility assessment of CPU-based tensor operations
limitations: Reproducibility reports have limited novelty; focuses on artifact evaluation rather than algorithmic innovation
